description:
Record money received against threads, in payments/<Kind>/<Thread>.md.

Subcommands:
  log THREAD AMOUNT [-c CURRENCY] [-d YYYY-MM-DD] [-t HH:MM] [-a ACCOUNT] [-n NOTE] [--all] — record a receipt.
  list [THREAD] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--json] — list payments.
  statement [--thread T] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--as-of YYYY-MM-DD] [--pdf PATH] [--json] — billed vs received, by thread and currency.
  show ID [--json] — show one payment.
  edit ID [--amount AMOUNT] [-c CURRENCY] [-d YYYY-MM-DD] [-t HH:MM] [-a ACCOUNT] [-n NOTE] — change fields of a payment.
  rm ID [-y] — delete a payment.

Flags:
  log: THREAD is a thread name, 'Kind/Name', or wikilink; AMOUNT is the amount received and must be positive. -c 3-letter ISO currency code, defaults to the thread's; -d date received, YYYY-MM-DD, default today; -t time, HH:MM, default now; -a which account it landed in; -n free-text note; --all applies only to interactive capture.
  statement: --thread limits to one thread; --since and --until bound the window; --as-of statement date, YYYY-MM-DD, drives aging, default today; --pdf renders a PDF to the given path and requires --thread; --json JSON output.
  rm: -y skips confirmation.

Examples:
  ["log", "Projects/SGB", "15000", "-d", "2026-09-10", "-a", "Current", "-n", "Invoice 42"]
  ["list", "Projects/SGB", "--json"]
  ["statement", "--thread", "Projects/SGB", "--as-of", "2026-09-30", "--json"]

Notes:
  Calling `log` with no THREAD enters interactive capture and reads from stdin — always pass THREAD and AMOUNT.
  `rm` without -y prompts for confirmation and permanently deletes the record.
  Money received must always name a currency; there is no unbilled mode as in `hours`.
  Amounts must be positive — a refund is not a negative payment.
  IDs are 8 hex chars, shared in one namespace with hours entry ids.
  `statement` counts billed time from `hours`; entries with no currency are ignored.
  Every recorded payment also drops a REF: into the buffer, filed under the date received, landing in the thread's daily log on the next `buffer flush`. Best-effort; the payment is recorded either way.
